column1: # clues.tsv for ft_find_next_prime — pedagogic hints only. NEVER state the expected value or the fix.
# Format: <hint><TAB><member CASE label><TAB>...   (fires if ANY member case fails)
# Lines are shown most-fundamental first; the first line doubles as the "foothold".
Read "next" carefully: is the search inclusive or strictly greater? When nb is already prime, must you move past it or can you return nb itself? Where does your scan start?

When nb is not prime, how do you reach the next one? You need a primality test you trust — could you reuse the same is-prime logic from the earlier exercise and just advance the candidate until it passes?
What is the smallest number that counts as prime? For any nb below that floor, what single value should every one of these collapse to?

For a candidate near the top of the int range, look hard at your loop bound itself, not just at nb. If you decide when to stop by squaring the divisor, is that product still representable? What other quantity could you compare the divisor against to ask the same question without ever building a value that big?
